headline: Growth accelerates as full-year guidance moves higher
summary_short: Labcorp reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.73 billion, up 5.8% y/y, with diluted EPS of $3.64 (+28.5% y/y) and adjusted EPS of $4.99 (+14.9% y/y); the company raised full-year 2026 revenue growth and adjusted EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 5.8% y/y to $3.731B, driven by 4.2% organic growth plus a modest contribution from acquisitions (net of divestitures) and FX. Diluted EPS rose 28.5% y/y to $3.64 and adjusted EPS grew 14.9% to $4.99, with adjusted operating margin expanding 70bps to 15.8% on organic growth and operating efficiencies. Free cash flow fell to $313.9M from $542.7M y/y on working-capital timing and planned capex increases. Labcorp retired $500M of senior notes, repurchased $353.8M of stock, and paid $58.7M in dividends, leaving cash at $141.8M (down from $647.3M) and total debt near $5.86B. The company raised FY2026 guidance: enterprise revenue growth to 5.4%-6.3% (from 5.0%-6.1%) and adjusted EPS to $18.10-$18.55 (from $17.70-$18.35); it also added $1.0B to its buyback authorization.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited 6% revenue growth, significant margin expansion, and double-digit adjusted EPS growth reflecting continued momentum, pointing to expanded oncology leadership and technology investments.
Growth was 4.2% organic plus 1.2 points from acquisitions net of divestitures and 0.4 points of FX; Diagnostics Laboratories, the largest segment, grew 5.5% to $2.901B.
Adjusted operating income and margin increased due to organic growth and operating efficiencies, per the release's own footnote on the 70bps AOI margin expansion.
EPS grew faster than net income (28.5% vs 25.6%) partly because diluted share count fell about 2.3% y/y on buybacks.
The release attributes the decline directly to working-capital timing and planned increases in capital expenditures.
